A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Q-RAG work. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original Q-RAG evaluations on BabiLong, RULER, HotPotQA, and MuSiQue, together with architectural ablations and sensitivity experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds retrieval-budget experiments, stopping-policy analyses, training curves, and additional QA results.

M1.justification: Appendix B adds a simulated Q-value-threshold early-stopping variant; v1 specified only a retrieval budget or generic STOP action. The embedding architecture, soft-Q training, temporal encoding, and existing Plan Q-RAG beam search are retained.

E1.justification: Table 1 adds RULER single-hop QA alongside the existing NIAH and multi-hop tasks. V2 also explicitly uses MuSiQue in joint training for the new GTE experiment, whereas v1 describes HotPotQA training and MuSiQue out-of-distribution evaluation. The benchmark families remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The new stopping analysis introduces an oracle stopping-policy reference in Figure 5. Evaluated comparator membership in Tables 1–3 remains unchanged. Search-o1 and HippoRAG have only empty rows in Table 7, which do not establish new evaluations.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 introduces a joint-trained GTE configuration, 1,000 HotPotQA examples, retrieval budgets of 2–5, and three Qwen3 answerers. Appendix B adds threshold sweeps and stopping-error metrics, excluding episodes whose full trajectories never recover all supporting chunks. These are substantial new evaluation designs; Appendix G's disclosures alone do not establish changes to existing experiments.

E4.justification: V2 adds retrieval-budget sensitivity, detailed early/late stopping-error analysis, threshold-dependent accuracy and retrieval-length comparisons, ROC curves, and training-convergence curves. The original architectural ablations and temperature/lambda sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same three-seed averages and identical plus/minus values in Table 3. The added experiments introduce no explicit new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises Q-RAG's multi-hop QA scores at 16K/32K/128K/1M from 67/67/62/57 to 64/65/65/61, and Beam Retriever's 4K/16K scores from 28.3/28.3 to 39/35. V2 adds single-hop QA, budget, stopping, in-distribution MuSiQue, and convergence results. Tables 2–3 retain their scores. These are revised and additional results, not evidence of an algorithmic performance gain.

T1.justification: Appendix A replaces the fixed-RoPE density argument with a variable-dimensional complex-diagonal theorem requiring a self-adjoint, point-separating positional algebra. The uniform rate with exponent s/(2dx+2dy+2) is replaced by an L2 rate with exponent s/(dx+dy+1), different assumptions, and new proofs. Separate uniform-bound conditions and Appendix D's complexity derivation are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: efficient embedder-only reinforcement learning, temporal retrieval reasoning, competitive QA, and strong long-context performance up to 10M tokens.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations of retrieval-budget versus noise tradeoffs, premature versus redundant retrieval, and threshold-dependent stopping failures. It also explains which components determine context-length scaling and distinguishes L2 approximation guarantees from stronger uniform guarantees requiring additional assumptions.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code link, statements about data/instructions and checkpoint availability, and detailed dataset-specific retrievers, chunk sizes, retrieval limits, and decoding settings. Appendix G clarifies that Fact EM means covering all supporting facts, allowing extra chunks; this documents the metric without establishing that its implementation changed. V1's optimizer and hardware details are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds MemUP to the recurrent-memory discussion and cites Malkov–Yashunin and Zhao et al. for approximate nearest-neighbor search. Birman–Solomyak and Novak–Wozniakowski disappear with the replaced proofs. The main positioning against retriever training, LLM training, and recurrent models remains stable.

P1.justification: Appendix A is substantially rewritten and reorganized into a real/complex reformulation, reordered lemma and theorem, staged derivations, and a uniform-bound discussion. Elsewhere, v2 promotes ablations to a standalone section, expands appendix organization, adds a reproducibility statement, and corrects terminology and cross-references. The main introduction and conclusion remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figures 4–6 and Tables 4–8 for stopping, budget, convergence, additional QA, and configurations. Table 1 gains separate single-hop and multi-hop QA columns. Existing Figures 2–3 retain their plotted content, while Figure 1 is resized.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially improves theoretical precision and reproducibility: Appendix A makes approximation assumptions and norm-dependent guarantees explicit, while Appendix G resolves important omissions about retrieval, generation, and Fact EM. Budget and stopping experiments address practical questions left untested in v1. These gains outweigh limited inconsistencies, including Appendix G's blanket QwQ-32B statement despite the Qwen3 answerers in Section 5.1. The improvement concerns evidence and documentation, not a demonstrated advance in the core algorithm.
